Overall, I think this delivers good value for the money, but the small D-ring bothers me. I think it might be too easy to dislodge the case.

Jerry

I've been using the wrist strap on my Fujifilm X100s for a couple years, and the included strap for my X-E2 is showing its age. Based on how much I liked the loop for my X100s, this purchase was a no brainer, and it's proven to be a wise one. Installation is a breeze, and the strap and included loops are very well made. I have zero concerns about securely holding my camera, even with Fuji's heavy glass onboard. The diameter of the rope is perfect, as its neither cartoonishly big nor so narrow it becomes a burden on my neck. If I wanted to use as a impromptu wristlet, I could easily wrap around my wrists without looking too ridiculous. The length is typical, which is what it is. Do note there's no way to adjust save for adding knots.

All of the above are well and all, but the main reason I bought this is that it looks sharp. I love the contrast, and it looks even better in person. As noted I've used the matching wrist strap on my smaller Fuji, and it looks as good today as a few years ago when new.

These are as good as a pair of basic headphones gets. They're comfortable, lightweight, and stylish. The sound quality is WAY better than the el-cheapo headphones you'll find included with just about all consumer electronics, but they're not quite as good as expensive, high-end headphones either. You don't give up a lot in terms of sound with these, so maybe they'd be the ones you want to wear out jogging, instead of your fancy, expensive, brand-name headphones, because at the price these aren't going to leave you heartbroken if they get lost, damaged, or stolen, and let's face it: You're not hearing all those finer points of your music while you're working out, huffing and puffing and grunting and groaning, anyway. Even if you don't work out, these are good everyday headphones that will deliver decent-quality music that will please most listeners.

The cord is sufficiently long, the pads are comfortable, and they're just plain good headphones. They aren't big-name super-bass expensive headphones, but considering the price, build quality, and sound quality, for their category they're definitely worthy of five stars.
